# Maintainer wiki: schema and writer brief

`documentation.wiki`. Owned by the house. The writer and the reviewer read this file first, every run.**

## The bar

Someone who knows nothing of this house but what the wiki holds can rebuild it. The wiki is for the builder; the
household reads the user manual (`docs/user-manual/`), which never carries entity ids.

## Hard rules for every writer

1. **Read-only on the house.** Read files and the API; never call a service, never write to the configuration,
   never send a message of any kind.
2. **No secrets in any page, source record or note:** no code, PIN, password, token, key, phone number, email or
   street address. Name a secret by its key ("the `alarm_panel_code` key in secrets.yaml"), never its value. Do not
   open the secrets file or the credential stores at all.
3. **Every factual claim carries a citation**, or is left out, or is marked `(unverified)`. Never invent a version,
   date, model number or behavior.
4. **Never type a fact the house can report.** Entity lists, counts, versions, states and dependencies come from
   the generated facts file (section 5); prose explains what they mean.
5. **The live export outranks prose.** When a page and the export disagree, the export wins and the page says so
   in one line, citing the export file.
6. **Stay in your own files.** A writer writes pages and their source records. The reviewer writes findings, never
   pages. Nobody hand-edits a generated file; fix the generator.

## Where things are

| Path | What | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `wiki/pages/<slug>.md` | the pages | the writer |
| `wiki/sources/<slug>.json` | each page's source records | the writer |
| `wiki/facts/<slug>.json` | generated facts, rebuilt from the live export | the facts generator only |
| `wiki/archive/<slug>/` | archived copies of every external source | the writer |
| `wiki/QUEUE.md` | pages to write or update, in order | the owner and sessions (add only) |
| `wiki/REVIEW.md` | the reviewer's findings, newest first | the reviewer |

(Large archives and the facts may live on a side branch instead; if so, say which here and keep the paths.)

## 1. Three kinds of page

- **Thing** (`type` names what it is: `integration`, `device`, `package`, `automation`, `dashboard`, `subsystem`,
  `hardware`, `cloud-service`): what it is, how it is configured, what it connects to, its lessons as short rules.
  No stories, no step lists.
- **Procedure** (`type: procedure`, slug starts with a verb: `restore-a-backup`): the steps and checks only.
- **Incident** (`type: incident`, slug starts with the date: `2026-01-15-leak-alert-never-arrived`): the story.

## 2. Front matter (every page)

```
---
title: Kitchen sink leak sensor
slug: kitchen-sink-leak-sensor
type: device
summary: One sentence that defines the subject for someone who has never seen the house.
status: In service since YYYY-MM-DD
categories: [Plumbing, Zigbee devices]
see_also: [plumbing-subsystem, zigbee]
verified: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

## 3. Sections, in order

- **Thing:** lead (one to three paragraphs, no heading; the subject in bold on first mention), `## Role in the
  house`, `## Configuration`, `## Interfaces`, `## History`, `## Lessons and gotchas`, `## Rebuild notes`,
  `## References`. Each lesson: a bold one-sentence rule, at most one sentence of why, its citation, and a link to
  the incident page if the story deserves one.
- **Procedure:** `## When to use this`, `## Before you start` (parts, versions, secrets by name, a backup),
  `## Steps` (numbered), `## Check it worked`, `## References`.
- **Incident:** `## What happened` (a timeline with times), `## Cause`, `## Fix`, `## Rule that came out of it`,
  `## References`. Its rule also goes into `docs/gotchas.md`.

## 4. Citations: one form

In the text, a footnote after the sentence: `...the sensor reports every 50 minutes when dry.[^2]`

In References, one per line, in exactly one of two forms:

```
[^2]: src:<source-id> <locator>
[^3]: page:<slug>#<passage-id>
```

The locator is a section, a line range, a page number or a short quoted phrase. `page:` cites a passage on another
page of the wiki; give passages a stable id with `{#p-<slug>-<name>}` at the end of the paragraph they mark. One
fact is stated in full on its own page; other pages cite it there rather than repeat it.

Every `src:` id is defined once in `wiki/sources/<slug>.json`, a JSON list of records:

```
[
 {"id": "config-leak-package", "kind": "repo-file", "title": "Plumbing package", "ref": "ha/packages/plumbing.yaml",
  "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"},
 {"id": "vendor-manual", "kind": "pdf", "title": "Leak sensor user manual, rev 2", "ref": "https://example.com/manual.pdf",
  "fetched": "YYYY-MM-DD", "archived_as": "archive/kitchen-sink-leak-sensor/manual-rev2.pdf",
  "sha256": "<hex>", "bytes": 123456, "license": "vendor, all rights reserved"}
]
```

`kind` is one of `repo-file`, `live-export`, `commit`, `note`, `web`, `pdf`, `package`. **Every `web`, `pdf` and
`package` source is archived** under `wiki/archive/<slug>/` with its sha256, size, fetch date and license: the
wiki must not depend on the original staying online. If a download fails, keep the record with
`"archived_as": null` and `"archive_error": "<why>"`; never drop the citation.

## 5. Generated facts

`wiki/facts/<slug>.json` is written by a script from the live export (entity ids, states, versions, config entry
names, which automations use the entity). The build renders it as the page's facts box, cited to the export
commit. A writer never types those values; if a fact the page needs is missing, add a line to `wiki/QUEUE.md` for
the generator, not a typed value.

## 6. The writer's run

1. Read this file, then `wiki/QUEUE.md`; take the first item not marked taken.
2. Read the live export for the subject, the CHANGELOG entries that name it, `docs/gotchas.md`, the design docs.
3. Write or update the page and its sources; archive every external source.
4. Check before finishing: every `[^n]` has a definition; every `src:` id exists; every `page:` target and passage
   id exists; no secret or phone number; links use slugs; front matter complete.
5. Report: files written, citations per page, archived files with sizes, anything `(unverified)`, anything not found.

## 7. The reviewer's run

Nightly, read-only: pick pages changed since the last review plus a few oldest-verified; check them against the
live export and their sources; write findings to `wiki/REVIEW.md` (page, claim, what the source says, suggested
fix). Never edit a page. A finding the writer disagrees with goes to the owner as a question.
